cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to God's people scattered across five regions (1 Peter 1:1). He's already told them the old crowd heaps abuse on them for not joining in the wild life anymore (1 Peter 4:4). Now he calls them 'Beloved' and names what they're going through: a fiery trial.

cards.question: Peter tells these believers to treat their fiery trial as something strange and unexpected.
Instead of being surprised by the fiery trial, Peter tells them to ___.
Peter tells these believers to rejoice in their fiery trial. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Their enemies will soon give up

cards.text: And sharing now leads somewhere: being overjoyed when His glory is revealed. Then Peter gets specific about one kind of suffering, being insulted for the name of Christ.

cards.question: Peter says a believer who is insulted for the name of Christ is blessed.
Why does Peter call the believer who is insulted for Christ's name blessed?

answers.text: The Spirit of glory rests on them
Their insulters will be punished at once
They will win the argument later

cards.text: Now Peter draws a line: none of them should suffer as a murderer, a thief, a wrongdoer, or even a meddler. MEDDLER made the list, friend, and I once stuck my mustache into a fight between the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with and got zapped from BOTH sides.

cards.question: But if they suffer as a Christian, Peter says not to be ___, and to glorify God that they bear that name.

cards.text: Then Peter turns the page, friend. It's time, he says, for judgment to begin.

cards.question: Peter says judgment begins with the ___ of God.
If judgment begins with God's family, what does Peter ask next?

answers.text: What awaits those who disobey the gospel
How long the judgment will last
Who will stand as the judge

cards.text: Then Peter adds a quote: "If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?"

cards.question: In the quote Peter adds, the ungodly and the sinner have an easier road than the righteous.

cards.text: So then. Peter's been building to this, and here it comes for everyone who suffers according to God's will.

cards.question: What does Peter say those who suffer according to God's will should do with their souls?

answers.text: Entrust them to their faithful Creator

cards.question: Peter says those who suffer according to God's will should stop doing good until the trial is over.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Suffering earns them God's favor' is close to something the passage says. Verse 14 says those insulted for the name of Christ are blessed, so a baker could argue this answer is right. Replace it with an answer that is clearly false anywhere in 1 Peter 4:12-19.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The right answer 'The Spirit of glory rests on them' sounds like Scripture. The wrong answer 'They will win the argument later' sounds casual and modern. The right answer stands out, so the answers should be rewritten to match in tone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new event from his time in the junk drawer: he stuck his mustache into a fight between the dead batteries and got zapped. The backstory mentions the batteries arguing, but not this incident. Jokes may only make up small moments around his bakery, not add new events to his backstory.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: 'Then Peter turns the page' presents verse 17 as a change of topic. In the BSB, verse 17 opens with 'For', which ties it to what comes before. The card should not decide how the two parts connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 8 has the only real joke in the walkthrough. The other story cards read flat, for example card 13 ('Then Peter adds a quote') and card 15 ('So then.'). Several cards have room for a laugh that doesn't blur a fact, such as cards 1, 5, 10 and 15. Papa Dorin's humor should come up naturally across the walkthrough.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
